### arjun (narrator: `baidu/ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free`)

Number check: 0 numbers not found in the aggregates.

> # Working with an AI assistant: Arjun, 2–13 November 2026
> 
> Between 2 and 13 November 2026 you worked with the assistant across 11 sessions on 10 active days, mostly in the afternoon (8 sessions) with 3 in the morning. All 11 sessions were in operations, and the recorded task types were 5 reports, 3 analysis tasks, and one each of decide, draft, and lookup. You used a skill in 7 of the 11 sessions — weekly-sales-report 4 times and inventory-reorder 3 times — and the assistant made 96 tool calls across 36 turns. Verification was recorded on 27 turns, of which 20 passed. Your side of the exchanges included 7 understanding questions, 4 refinements, 3 feedback relays, and 1 correction, with no reexplanations requested. One example from the period records the assistant failing to draft the order email after grouping reorder items by supplier.
> 
> ## Questions to reflect on
> 
> - When the order email draft failed after items were grouped by supplier, what signal told you it had gone wrong, and how early did you see it?
> - You asked 7 understanding questions and requested no reexplanations — which answers were still unclear to you after the first explanation?
> 
> ## Suggestions
> 
> - Split the inventory-reorder work into two requests: one for grouping items by supplier, and a separate one for the email draft, so a failure in the first does not hold up the second.
> - State the check you want in the first request (for example, comparing net revenue with the previous week, or adding AOV and top products) instead of arriving as a later refinement, given that 20 of 27 verified turns passed.

> **Reflection report – Lena (2 to 13 November 2026)**  
> 
> Lena completed 8 sessions across 7 active days, all occurring in the evening.  
> The sessions contained 25 turns, including 6 refinements and 8 understanding questions.  
> She made 1 correction and no feedback relays or reexplanations.  
> Tool calls totaled 68, and 6 of the 8 sessions involved a skill such as weekly‑sales‑report (used 4 times) or price‑change‑memo (used once).  
> Verified turns passed were 15 out of 15, and the work spanned domains like operations (3), strategy (2), support (2), and writing (1).  
> 
> ### Questions to reflect on
> 1. How did the concentration of all sessions in the evening influence the depth of the refinements?  
> 2. What prompted the single correction, and could a feedback relay have captured that insight earlier?  
> 
> ### Suggestions
> 1. Schedule at least one session in a different part of the day to test whether varied timing changes the number of understanding questions.  
> 2. Enable the feedback relay feature for future sessions to automatically log corrections and reduce the need for manual tracking.
